nodes.label: Client Offboarding and Data Retention Spec
nodes.norm_label: client offboarding and data retention spec

nodes.label: Decision: PostgreSQL as the single persistent store
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL carries relational data, the job queue, and vector embeddings because cost-efficient-operation.md forbids tenant-independent fixed-cost infrastructure and every additional always-on backing service (a dedicated broker, a dedicated vector DB) is exactly that; one store is also cheapest to make identical across laptop, VPS, and managed cloud.
nodes.norm_label: decision: postgresql as the single persistent store

nodes.label: Decision: Node 24 native TypeScript type stripping, no build step
nodes.rationale: Node 24 executes .ts directly, so the source tree is the artifact, giving environment-portability.md's 'byte-for-byte identical artifact' requirement a trivially provable meaning; cost is erasableSyntaxOnly must stay on, so no enum, namespace, or constructor parameter properties.
nodes.norm_label: decision: node 24 native typescript type stripping, no build step

nodes.label: Decision: Ports-and-adapters for every external dependency
nodes.rationale: AI provider, WhatsApp transport, object storage, queue, and clock are each a port with at least one real adapter and one in-memory fake, which is what makes ai-provider-portability.md and component-independence.md testable rather than aspirational.
nodes.norm_label: decision: ports-and-adapters for every external dependency

nodes.label: Decision: Tenant isolation enforced in the database via row-level security
nodes.rationale: Every tenant-scoped table carries tenant_id and RLS policies bind reads/writes to a session-scoped tenant context, because tenant-data-isolation.md requires an identifier belonging to tenant A be useless in tenant B's context 'even if guessed, reused, or supplied out of context' -- an application-layer WHERE clause fails open the first time someone forgets it.
nodes.norm_label: decision: tenant isolation enforced in the database via row-level security

nodes.label: Decision: Hand-written PostgreSQL client
nodes.rationale: @zeddev/db implements protocol v3 directly over node:net/tls (SCRAM-SHA-256, extended and simple query flow, LISTEN/NOTIFY) instead of a driver dependency, because every dependency is a supply-chain and maintenance cost against a near-zero-fixed-cost premise, and the wire protocol has been stable since 2003; every path is tested against a real PostgreSQL since there is no fake server in the package.

nodes.label: Decision: Round-robin tenant-fair queue dispatch
nodes.rationale: Queue dispatch is round-robin across tenants via a per-(queue, tenant) cursor rather than a global FIFO, because message-delivery-reliability.md forbids one tenant's backlog delaying another's and cost-efficient-operation.md forbids a queue per tenant; an in-flight cap covers a hung handler occupying every worker.

nodes.label: Decision: Configured list of sealing keys for tenant secrets
nodes.rationale: tenant_secrets are sealed under a configured list of keys (VAULT_SEALING_KEYS) rather than one key, so rotation (credential-and-secret-handling.md AC8, AC9) is a configuration change rather than a flag day: values sealed under a retired id keep unsealing as long as that id is still listed.
nodes.norm_label: decision: configured list of sealing keys for tenant secrets

nodes.label: Decision: Tagged first-line reply output protocol
nodes.rationale: The reply output protocol is a tagged first line ([reply]/[handoff]/[fallback]) rather than JSON, because free text with quotes and emoji is escaped less reliably inside JSON by small free-tier models and JSON mode is not exposed by the port; untagged output with no tag anywhere is still accepted as a reply so formatting obedience is not conflated with answer quality.
nodes.norm_label: decision: tagged first-line reply output protocol

nodes.label: Decision: Readiness defined once in SQL with triggers
nodes.rationale: CHECK (NOT active OR ready) on bot_activation plus AFTER triggers on every readiness input (whatsapp_connections, bot_personas) re-evaluate in the same transaction, because an application-level 'remember to call reevaluate' would fail open the first time a new path (gateway, scheduler, offboarding) forgot to call it.
nodes.norm_label: decision: readiness defined once in sql with triggers

nodes.label: Decision: Four-step WhatsApp connection verification state machine
nodes.rationale: Connection is earned by a round trip (authorize, submit, send a one-time code, reply with it) with CONNECTION_TRANSITIONS having no edge into connected except from connecting, because whatsapp-number-connection.md is explicit that submitted credentials alone must never produce a 'connected' state.
nodes.norm_label: decision: four-step whatsapp connection verification state machine

nodes.label: Decision: cloudFailureDeterminacy for retry-without-duplication
nodes.rationale: A failed WhatsApp send is classified none (Meta answered, so repeating is safe) or unknown (default), because message-delivery-reliability.md AC7 requires both retry and no duplication and the Cloud API offers no idempotency key or after-the-fact send status; guessing 'none' incorrectly is how a customer gets the same reply twice.

nodes.label: Decision: Migrations are forward-only
nodes.rationale: No down scripts; a rollback script is written when the schema is understood and executed when it is not, and 'roll back the migration' on a table holding tenant data means deleting that data. Recovering from a bad migration is a new forward migration.

nodes.label: Decision: Log redaction as an allowlist
nodes.rationale: src/lib/logging permits only field names in OPERATIONAL_FIELDS and replaces everything else with [redacted], because a denylist fails open the first time a field is named body or pw; log calls take a dotted event name rather than a free-text message string so there is no channel to interpolate content into.
nodes.norm_label: decision: log redaction as an allowlist

nodes.label: Decision: Hand-written SigV4 signer and HTTP client
nodes.rationale: The SigV4 signer and the HTTP client for object storage are hand-written, node:http/https rather than fetch (fetch adds headers underneath a signature), on the same reasoning as the PostgreSQL client: SigV4 is a published, frozen algorithm with official test vectors and the AWS SDK is several hundred packages.
nodes.norm_label: decision: hand-written sigv4 signer and http client

nodes.label: Decision: node:test and npm workspaces, zero test/build dependencies
nodes.rationale: node:test is the test runner and npm workspaces the package manager, because every dependency is a supply-chain and maintenance cost carried on a platform whose whole premise is near-zero fixed cost, and pnpm is not installed on the target machine.
nodes.norm_label: decision: node:test and npm workspaces, zero test/build dependencies
